recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. If future work wants a mandatory or recommended reciprocal link between DocumentReference and DiagnosticReport, it should be raised as a new work-group decision because FHIR-25243 did not approve that requirement.
issue_request: FHIR-25243 asked core FHIR to clarify the overlap between DocumentReference and DiagnosticReport and to define a designated way for duplicated resources representing the same document to refer to each other. The final Published disposition was Not Persuasive with Modification: it rejected a core requirement to create paired DocumentReference/DiagnosticReport instances and required only changing the DiagnosticReport introductory bullet from "Other diagnostics - Cardiology, Gastroenterology etc." to "Other diagnostics such as Cardiology, Gastroenterology etc."
initial_application: No git commit explicitly names FHIR-25243, but the July 2020 OO block vote that included the issue was followed by commit 0bf0b46a829ce94829ceef7e036dcb2043c74d18, "DocumentReference block vote from July," which changed source/diagnosticreport/diagnosticreport-introduction.xml to "Other diagnostics such as Cardiology, Gastroenterology, etc." The current active DiagnosticReport source still contains that wording.
additional_context: The linked Zulip thread shows implementer confusion about PDF reports, DiagnosticReport.presentedForm, DocumentReference, and whether systems should create both resources. Later final issues FHIR-19250 and FHIR-19249 addressed the broader boundary/overlap question by adding reciprocal DiagnosticReport/DocumentReference boundary text, without creating a mandatory cross-link rule. Current DiagnosticReport.media.link can target DocumentReference, and current DocumentReference.related can point to related resources, but FHIR-25243 did not approve a requirement that duplicated report resources always reference each other.
reconciliation: Published empty audit commit 808fff2906adc1ec6141c4e3f646b6b26749caed. No source edit was made because the required DiagnosticReport wording is already present and later boundary prose already explains the overlap consistently with the no-mandatory-link decision.
